newsitem.title: USA: Iomega to cut up to 700 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Iomega to cut up to 700 jobs.

text.p: Iomega Corp. said Monday up to 700 jobs at its Roy, Utah, plants will be cut because the data storage device company plans to increase production at its Penang, Malaysia, plant.
The Roy, Utah-based company said the moves, which will also include relocating its European headquarters, will result in a one-time charge of $10 million for its fourth quarter.
Iomega said its Penang operations have reached volume production faster than expected and are now equipped to produce all types of Iomega's personal storage products, including the popular Zip drive.
As a result, Iomega said it will eliminate 500 to 700 positions at its Utah facilities in production, manufacturing and distribution, beginning in March.
The Roy, Utah-based company said affected employees will be offered help getting new jobs, extensions of medical benefits, and severance packages.

"Moving manufacturing operations to Penang gets us closer to our storage component suppliers, ultimately lowering the cost of handling and shipping inventory," Chief Operating Officer Wayne Stewart said in a statement. "This strategy will benefit our customers by driving product costs down."
Iomega said it plans to transfer manufacturing facilities at Roy to Penang throughout the first half of 1997.

The Utah facility will remain Iomega's worldwide headquarters and will house research and development, strategic procurement, finance and accounting, administration, sales and marketing and distrubution, beginning in March.

Iomega also said that in order to improve responsiveness to customers in Europe, it plans in early 1997 to move its European management, sales and marketing to Geneva and its European logistics and distribution to Utrecht, Netherlands.
Iomega's stock closed at $16.50, down 87.5 cents a share, on the New York Stock Exchange. The company announced the move after stock trading closed.
